questions.q: Should restaurants respond to every review?
questions.a: Yes, it's worth responding to both positive and negative reviews. Answering only the good ones makes it look like you avoid criticism, and an unanswered complaint lets the reviewer have the final say. Your replies are public, so they also show future guests how you treat people.

questions.q: How do I respond to a negative restaurant review?
questions.a: Start by thanking the guest for taking the time to write, then talk to your team to understand what happened. If you got something wrong, own it without excuses, apologize and invite the guest back. Offer a phone number or email so you can continue the conversation privately.

questions.q: How do I respond to a positive restaurant review?
questions.a: Thank the guest warmly and mention the specific thing they enjoyed, so the reply feels personal. You can recommend a dish they haven't tried yet and invite them back. A short, genuine reply turns a happy guest into a returning one.

questions.q: How quickly should I reply to a restaurant review?
questions.a: Reply as soon as you reasonably can. A swift response shows you pay attention and value honest feedback, while a slow one can leave the reviewer feeling ignored. Take a moment to stay calm and proofread before posting, since the reply goes out under your brand's name.

questions.q: How can I prevent bad restaurant reviews?
questions.a: There are no legal ways to get honest negative reviews deleted, so focus on giving guests fewer reasons to complain. Run regular audits of the experience, check on diners during the meal and fix the issues that come up repeatedly. Asking happy guests for feedback and reviews before they leave helps your rating reflect the experience most people have.
